Surely, &c.--</hi>The form is that of an oath or strongest assertion. Submission is denoted by the figure of a weaned child. As the child weaned by his mother from the breast, so I still the motions of pride in me (<reference osisRef="Matt.18.3">Mt 18:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.18.4">4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.11.8">Is 11:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.28.9">28:9</reference>). Hebrew children were often not weaned till three years old.<div eID="gen10797" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10798" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">soul--</hi>may be taken for desire, which gives a more definite sense, though one included in the idea conveyed by the usual meaning, myself. <chapter eID="Ps.131"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. Surely, &c.-- The form is that of an oath or strongest assertion. Submission is denoted by the figure of a weaned child. As the child weaned by his mother from the breast, so I still the motions of pride in me ( Mt 18:3 , 4 ; Is 11:8 ; 28:9 ). Hebrew children were often not weaned till three years old. soul-- may be taken for desire, which gives a more definite sense, though one included in the idea conveyed by the usual meaning, myself.
